The raw_merchants table holds 46 rows for 40 distinct merchant_ids. Six merchant_ids appear twice, and the copies are identical in every column, so the duplicates are exact. The join in gold_mcc_daily therefore fans out and inflates the count from 4558 to 5256.

The fix is to deduplicate in silver_merchants with SELECT DISTINCT. The copies are identical, so this loses no information and keeps the same columns. As a safeguard, I could use GROUP BY merchant_id with min(mcc), but DISTINCT is enough here because the copies do not differ.

The other tables are unaffected: gold_merchant_daily and gold_customer_spend do not use merchants. The customers table is unique, so gold_region_daily is fine.

As a check on the numbers, six duplicated merchants adding 698 extra rows is plausible, at roughly 116 rows per merchant.

The only step that needs replacing is silver_merchants, and gold_mcc_daily will be correct once it reruns.
